blocks.text: The bar: a place's look is its film stock graded over the frame, never repainted. A look never relights or brightens a room: day, dusk and weather move the sun and swap the sky, a dark room gets more from its lights (→atmosphere); exposure is the stock, not the lamp. Moonlight is uniform ops (exposure down, cool tint, blue vignette), never a grade keyed on a colour, luminance or depth threshold, which fringes blended silhouettes pale. A night keeps its blacks, its grade moving mids and colour. The ground stays readable under any grade.

look(ctx) runs over the finished tone-mapped frame (scene, bloom, outlines) before sRGB encoding. Verbs: spawn api builtin/postfx, world-point queries builtin/lighting. From run_script, ctx.place.atmosphere.look = … is live, null resets. A behavior's look.params.density = 0.6 is free; a script or pass edit recompiles once: per-frame change rides params.

// scripts/look-place.js import { grade, grain, vignette } from "builtin/postfx"; export function look(ctx) { const c = grade(ctx.scene, { exposure: 1.05, saturation: 1.1, temperature: 0.1, haze: 0.06 }); return grain(vignette(c, ctx.param("vignette", 0.25), { color: "oklch(0.121 0.019 283.1)" }), 0.05); }
Haze in the grade is the air. Moody: saturation toward 0.55, exposure just under 1, deeper vignette.
Glow is the lights, never the room: bloomThreshold stays at 1 (under 1, lit walls and faces bloom), bloomStrength unset till an ask names glow (0 skips its passes).
A beam is fx (→fx). Fog you walk through (mist, shafts, lamp halos) is a march on high and ultra; below, fog.height is the air:

// scripts/look-mist.js, yours import { vec2, vec3, vec4, float, Loop, mix, select, mx_noise_float, cameraPosition, screenUV, time, deltaTime } from "builtin/tsl"; import { sunDirection, sunRadiance, ambientRadiance, sunVisibility, lightsAt, windTravel } from "builtin/lighting"; export function look(ctx) { if (!["high", "ultra"].includes(ctx.device.quality)) return ctx.scene; const size = { width: 640, height: 360 }, air = ctx.target("air", size), mist = ctx.target("mist", size); const reach = (uv) => { const ray = ctx.worldPosition(uv).sub(cameraPosition); return ray.normalize().mul(ray.length().min(60)); }; const now = ctx.pass(air, (uv) => { const ray = reach(uv), dir = ray.normalize(), dt = ray.length().div(16); const start = uv.mul(air.size).dot(vec2(0.0671, 0.0058)).fract().mul(52.98).add(time.mul(7.31)).fract(); const toSun = dir.dot(sunDirection).mul(0.5).add(0.5).pow(4).mul(0.6); const wind = vec3(windTravel.x, 0, windTravel.y), light = vec3(0).toVar(), clear = float(1).toVar(); Loop(16, ({ i }) => { const p = cameraPosition.add(dir.mul(float(i).add(start).mul(dt))); const fog = ctx.param("density", 0.08).mul(p.y.max(0).div(-2.5).exp()).mul(mx_noise_float(p.sub(wind).mul(0.2)).add(1)); const through = fog.mul(dt).negate().exp(); light.addAssign(sunRadiance.mul(sunVisibility(p)).mul(toSun).add(ambientRadiance.add(lightsAt(p, { shadow: false })).mul(0.1)).mul(clear).mul(float(1).sub(through))); clear.mulAssign(through); }); return vec4(light, clear); }); const fog = ctx.pass(mist, (uv) => { const at = ctx.previousUv(cameraPosition.add(reach(uv))), seen = at.sub(0.5).abs().lessThanEqual(0.5).all(); let n = now.sample(uv), lo = n, hi = n; for (const [x, y] of [[-1, -1], [1, -1], [-1, 1], [1, 1]]) { const s = now.sample(uv.add(vec2(x, y).div(air.size))); lo = lo.min(s); hi = hi.max(s); } return mix(select(seen, mist.previous.sample(at).clamp(lo, hi), n), n, float(1).sub(deltaTime.mul(-6.5).exp())); }).sample(screenUV); return ctx.scene.mul(fog.w).add(fog.rgb); }
A pass is for what only the finished frame says: a trail is mix(t.previous.sample(uv.sub(ctx.velocity)).rgb, ctx.scene, persist) written back into its target.
A thing drawn at lower resolution (pixel hands) is a see-through copy following it whose transparent material reads viewportSharedTexture at each n-pixel cell's centre: only it goes blocky.

Edges are two facts a pixel apart: ctx.viewZAt(uv) steps at a silhouette, ctx.normal(uv) turns at a crease; ink is max(smoothstep(0.03, 0.06, dz.div(abs(zc).max(1))), smoothstep(0.2, 0.5, dn)) mixed toward dark over the whole frame, land included; one object's ink is its material's outline (spawn api material). 1-bit is luminance against a 4×4 Bayer threshold; a screen-door fade drops pixels into the sky through the dither by ctx.viewZ, never a soft blend.
Decals make a place lived in: emit("decal", { position, normal, texture, size, lifetime, attachTo }); lifetime: Infinity keeps a mark for good.
emit("decal", { position, normal, texture, size, lifetime, attachTo })
Lighting: what a light does to a surface

Built once before the look, lighting colours each lit pixel before emissive and fog. The starter's scripts/lighting.js is the standard model: read, then edit. Flat is one tint per facing (step(0.5, n.y)); hatching is screenUV × screenSize diagonals where light falls off:

// scripts/lighting.js: toon bands import { dot, ceil, clamp } from "builtin/tsl"; export function lighting(surface, lights, ctx) { const bands = ctx.param("bands", 3), direct = lights.each((light) => { const band = ceil(clamp(dot(surface.normal, light.direction), 0, 1).mul(bands)).div(bands); return surface.albedo.mul(light.color).mul(band).mul(light.shadow); }); return direct.add(surface.albedo.mul(lights.ambient).add(lights.environment).mul(surface.occlusion)); }

light.shadow multiplies in after the bands, never inside a step: it fades far and under cloud, so a threshold on it or its product draws a line on the ground. A crisp shadow is the light's shadow.softness: 0 (sun: atmosphere.sun.light). A failed compile keeps the standard model. A material script may export lighting(surface, lights, ctx) beside material(ctx): its surfaces shade through it, whatever lit material it returns, with its uv(), positionLocal and ctx, so its pattern sticks.

surface: { albedo: vec3, normal: vec3, geometryNormal: vec3, view: vec3, position: vec3, roughness: f32, metalness: f32, occlusion: f32, attribute: f32 } // the material at this pixel, world space: position in world metres (positionWorld); normal and view unit, view toward the camera; geometryNormal before any normal map (noon relief: normal against it); attribute the face's integer kind, a lamp or a pane (ctx.attribute or m.attributeNode rounded, else 0), never a material value lights.each((light) => vec3): vec3 // summed over the sun and each placed light reaching the point, with falloff and cone. light = { direction: vec3 (toward it), color: vec3 (× intensity × falloff), shadow: f32 (0..1, 1 lit), radiance: vec3 (color × shadow), specular: f32 (0..1), isSun: bool (sun or moon) } lights.ambient: vec3, lights.environment: vec3 // irradiance at the normal from the place's ambient and hemisphere lights, else a colour or gradient sky's; a realistic sky's light as this surface returns it (albedo and reflection in) when the place sets neither (else black) ctx.device, ctx.quality // in lighting() and look() as in a material (`spawn api builtin/three`); a device its passes slow draws the "low" build: what matters, without costly passes (no branch: occlusion 1, glow 0); ctx.device.hold 0..1, this viewer's share of full device memory: scale counts by it export function look(ctx): vec3 | vec4 // once at build atmosphere.look.toneMapping: "aces" (default) filmic | "neutral" keeps painted hue and saturation, mids darker | "agx" | "reinhard" | "cineon" | "linear" | "none" clamped 0..1 (grade's `exposure` only multiplies), for display colours // agx costs ≤1.25x aces, ≤2.75x in ink/display(); a look may carry only this atmosphere.look.filter: "pixel" // blocks: drawn under screen size, each pixel stays one hard square ctx.scene: vec3 // this pixel; other pixels: convertToTexture(ctx.scene).sample(uv), in a pass texture(ctx.scene, uv) ctx.depth: texture, ctx.viewZ: float // raw depth (sky 0), .sample(uv) anywhere; linear, negative metres ctx.viewZAt(uv): float, ctx.normal(uv): vec3 // viewZ at uv (y down from top-left); the facet's normal from depth (sky faces the eye); { shading: true } the lit normal, smooth over a body's triangles ctx.worldPosition(uv): vec3 // the visible surface's point, sky the far plane; all three take (uv, { liquid: true }) for a liquid's surface, not its bed ctx.skyVisibility(P, N?): float // a world's lighting() too: 0..1 sky at P through blocks: 1 open, 0 under blocks or ground, between under leaves or liquid; models cast none; N the normal, none for air ctx.previousUv(P): vec2 // P's uv last frame, else (-1, -1) ctx.velocity: vec2 // this pixel's uv now − uv last frame from the eye's motion: a moving thing may read still, a still capture 0; motion blur samples back along it ctx.param(name, default): node // atmosphere.sky.params.<name> live, the viewer's layer (player.<path>, one screen) over the place's; a material script's reads its own params. Compose in node space (float(1).sub(dim)): JS arithmetic on it is NaN, which the passes refuse ctx.texture(cdn, { wrap: "clamp" | "repeat" | "mirror" }): texture // a LUT strip; clamp (default) smears the edge texel past uv 1: repeat ctx.target(name, { scale, width, height, depth, format: "rgba16float" | "rgba8unorm", wrap }): target // canvas scale (above 1 supersamples) or pixel width and height; rgba16float the HDR default, no tone-map or clamp between passes; .previous last frame's (first black), .size a live vec2 in pixels; depth makes it 3D (uv, .sample, .size vec3), filled once when its pass reads only uv and params ctx.pass(target, (uv) => vec3 | vec4): texture // runs in declaration order, overwriting its target; returns the read (.sample(uv), .size); reads t.previous, never its own target player.look.push(script | { look, intensity, duration, fade, priority, params }): length // one player's own look (fog only they see), same script, params whole: spread the place's under theirs; id: player.look.at(-1).id; duration auto-clears; higher priority wins
